newFindings.blocking: must fix or explicitly acknowledge before approval
newFindings.title: Other pending requirements contradict the corrected C64 and SX-64 port wiring
newFindings.detail: FR-CPU-004 ac-03 says Bit 3 controls the cassette motor (active low) and ac-05 says Bit 5 is unused on C64; FR-PRF-003 ac-02/ac-04 say SX-64 cassette sense always reads no tape and bit 4 is permanently pulled high. Pinned VICE drives the motor from bit 5, writes on bit 3, reads input bit 5 as 0, and on SX-64 reads input bits 3-5 as 0. The amendment corrects FR-TAP-001 and adds SX-64 behavior to FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 but leaves these contradictions, so the corpus would hold mutually unsatisfiable criteria. The existing FrCpu004AcceptanceTests.cs:67-90 already asserts bit 5 under the name PortBit3_ControlsTheCassetteMotorActiveLow and documents that the FR text is wrong. The prior review F-05 statement that FR-TAP-001 was the only C64 motor wiring requirement was inaccurate.
newFindings.evidence: Live FR-CPU-004 ac-03/ac-05 and FR-PRF-003 ac-02/ac-04 (pending, unsatisfied); c64pla.c:61-63, 65-67, 77-89; c64mem.c:218-222 (SX-64 config 1,1,1,1,0x07).
newFindings.recommendation: Add exact corrections for FR-CPU-004 ac-03/ac-05 and FR-PRF-003 ac-02/ac-04 in an expanded delta for explicit approval, or have the operator explicitly accept a recorded open contradiction with a tracked follow-up before this approval.

newFindings.blocking: must fix before approval (AC wording and named case)
newFindings.title: The second entry point of the ordinary start helper is not specified or tested
newFindings.detail: datasette_start_motor runs on a stopped-motor motor-on transition and also when START, FORWARD or REWIND is accepted while the motor already runs (with and without an image). That path schedules the 32000-cycle startup alarm when none is pending and seeds last_write_clk/last_write_bit. FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-03 describes ordinary startup only for a stopped motor, and no named case covers PLAY pressed with the motor already on (for example the C64 DDR-input motor-on state after reset). A mock that schedules startup only on motor transitions passes every named case.
newFindings.recommendation: State both entry points in FR-RUNTIME-TAPE-002 ac-03 and TR-TAPE-EDGE-001 ac-01 and add a named case such as Start_CommandWhileMotorRunning with pending and no-pending alarm variants.

newFindings.title: Hidden process-lifetime native state is not required to be pinned
newFindings.detail: Expected observations depend on state not reset by attach, detach or reset: tape wobble is on by default (3 Hz, 0.5 percent) with function-static wobble_sin_count/restf advanced even by the attach-time full-image gap scan; azimuth error draws lib_unsigned_rand when nonzero; last_write_bit starts at -1; C64 old_port_* statics start at 0xff and survive pport reset; VIA reset sets oldpb=0 while the effective PB output is 0xFF; datasette sound ring and sign statics; CP Clock F83 RTC wall clock. The criteria require identical resource state but do not require pinning or neutralizing these hidden states (only TR-TAP-EDGE-001 ac-05 names wobble/azimuth for the live decode path).
newFindings.evidence: datasette.c:86, 436-502, 897-901; datasette.h:58-74; c64pla.c:40-46, 106-123; viacore.c:378-424; datasette-sound.c:36-45; cp-clockf83.c:86-108.
newFindings.recommendation: Name hidden static state and wobble/azimuth/speed resources in the fixture/provider contract (or pin them to neutral values) before writing mocks.

newFindings.title: Attach, detach and reset quirks are not enumerated
newFindings.detail: Attach and reset set motor_stop_clk=0 without clearing datasette_motor, cancelling a pending delayed stop and leaving the motor running indefinitely; a stale read alarm survives attach because internal_reset inspects the new image STOP mode; detach and no-image reset re-apply the stale notape_mode command, which can schedule fast-wind or startup alarms and transiently assert sense before attach clears it. Only the generic Datasette_AttachDetachResetState group covers this.
newFindings.recommendation: Enumerate these cases in the lifecycle group.

newFindings.title: Recording file position depends on command order
newFindings.detail: fseek happens only in datasette_start_motor. RECORD accepted while the motor already runs performs no fseek, so writes go to the stdio position left by earlier buffered reads, and C requires a positioning call between input and output on update streams. FR-TAP-004 ac-04 existing-image current-position recording could bind to platform-dependent native behavior.
newFindings.recommendation: Decide in the fixture design whether this ordering is in scope and how the native oracle is pinned.

newFindings.title: Unknown TAP versions and the minimum-size rejection are not enumerated
newFindings.detail: The header reader stores any version byte; the block decoder returns 0 for a zero byte without consuming an extension for versions other than 0, 1 and 2, while the live path consumes a three-byte extension for any version of 1 or more. tap_open also ignores the declared data length and rejects images with fewer than 3 data bytes.
newFindings.recommendation: Name these cases under FR-TAP-002 ac-04/ac-08 or record them as explicit scope decisions.

verifiedNativeFacts: Start helper schedules startup only when no datasette alarm is pending and is reached from motor-on and from START/FORWARD/REWIND with the motor running (datasette.c:1000-1021, 1065-1089, 1123-1147, 1186-1190)
Motor-off sets the deadline once and arms an alarm only when none is pending; motor-on clears the deadline without restarting a running motor (datasette.c:1182-1205)
The callback stops the motor only when clk >= deadline; active reading replaces the same alarm (datasette.c:729-751, 806-851; alarm.h:176-183)
STOP leaves a pending alarm in place (datasette.c:1052-1058)
FORWARD/REWIND assign mode first, then arm clk+1000 regardless of motor (datasette.c:925-949, 1069-1090)
Writes require image, RECORD mode and motor flag plus a 0 to nonzero edge; line value always retained (datasette.c:1303-1321)
Accepted RECORD resets last_write_clk without the start helper (datasette.c:1091-1099, 1035-1038)
Gap encoding: below 7 carried, 7..2046 one byte (7 emits 0x00), 2047+ zero byte plus low 24 bits for v1/v2, failures stop the tape (datasette.c:1215-1291)
C64 motor !(DDR&DATA&0x20), write (~DDR|DATA)&0x08, sense input bit 4, SX-64 forwarding disabled and inputs 3-5 read 0 (c64pla.c:61-96; c64mem.c:218-222)
VIC-20 motor from raw changed PCR bit 1, write from effective PB3 including DDRB writes, sense VIA1 PA6 (vic20via1.c:188-198, 246-251; vic20via2.c:115-117; viacore.c:717-724)
Read pulses: C64 CIA1 FLAG, VIC-20 VIA2 CA1 falling (c64datasette.c:36-41; vic20datasette.c:37-42)
tapeinit CBM bands 36-54, 55-73, 74-100 after tap_init /8; TurboTape bands 10-34 and 35-54 unchanged (c64.c:231-248; vic20.c:267-284; tap.c:52-82, 1673-1680)

Block decoder v0 zero = 256 units, v1/v2 zero = 24-bit extension >>3, v2 sums halfwaves; live path byte*8, v0 zero = DatasetteZeroGapDelay, then wobble and misalignment (tap.c:389-444; datasette.c:504-535)

Header: short read or bad magic rejected; tag/video mismatches warn; Plus4 mismatch logs error without rejection; declared length ignored on open; fewer than 3 data bytes rejected (tap.c:121-197, 218-265)
Datasette audio is a separate sound chip with a 200-entry gap ring, flushed when DatasetteSound is off (default 0) (datasette-sound.c:36-76; datasette.c:270-295, 839-841)
